paragraphs: BrainODE models how brain shape changes over time, with the aim of supporting early prediction of neurodegenerative disease progression. Longitudinal brain scans present a difficult learning problem: datasets can be small, visits occur at uneven intervals, and people differ substantially. The framework represents deformation across anatomically meaningful regions rather than treating future shape prediction as an isolated output.

Its central component is a conditional neural ordinary differential equation, which describes shape evolution continuously through time. Subject age and cognitive status condition those dynamics. To forecast from a single observation, BrainODE also introduces an embedding representing predicted cognitive status. This lets it progressively predict intermediate shapes while incorporating predicted cognitive decline into later steps.

Experiments report better future brain shape predictions than time-aware baselines and strong generalization across longitudinal datasets with regular and irregular observation intervals. The findings support the framework’s usefulness for modeling evolving morphology under varied sampling schedules. Its reported evidence concerns shape forecasting, which is the mechanism proposed to support disease progression prediction.
neurips-2025-brainode-neural-shape-dynam.tldr: BrainODE uses continuous, age- and cognition-conditioned dynamics to forecast brain shape changes from a single observation.

paragraphs: CHASM examines whether multimodal language models can recognize advertisements disguised as ordinary social media posts. The central difficulty is that a genuine account of using a product may closely resemble covert promotion. Evaluating this distinction requires examples where promotional intent cannot be inferred simply from the presence of a product or an enthusiastic description.

The authors assemble 4,992 manually curated, anonymized instances based on real-world scenarios from Rednote, a Chinese social media platform. Collection and annotation follow privacy protection and quality control protocols. The dataset deliberately includes product experience posts that resemble hidden advertisements, making the evaluation sensitive to the distinction that moderators actually need to make.

In the reported zero-shot and in-context evaluations, none of the tested models was sufficiently reliable. Fine-tuning open-source models on CHASM produced noticeable gains, but subtle comment cues and differences in visual and textual structure remained challenging. The accompanying error analysis identifies where detection breaks down, positioning the dataset as a benchmark for improving moderation of disguised commercial content.
neurips-2025-chasm-unveiling-covert-adve.tldr: CHASM provides a challenging Rednote dataset showing that covert advertising remains difficult for multimodal models to detect reliably.

paragraphs: ControlFusion addresses image fusion when the source images suffer from multiple degradations at once. The problem is both restorative and interactive: the system must combine useful visual information while accommodating different degradation levels and user preferences. A fixed fusion procedure offers limited flexibility when these conditions change.

The authors first build a degradation simulator grounded in imaging mechanisms, including Retinex theory and atmospheric scattering. This supplies examples of compound degradation. They then design a restoration and fusion network whose feature enhancement changes according to degradation prompts. A text encoder translates user descriptions of degradation types and severity into inputs that control this processing.

The framework also includes a visual adapter that examines spatial and frequency information to infer degradation directly from the images. This reduces dependence on users describing every problem correctly. Experiments report better fusion quality and degradation handling than state-of-the-art fusion methods, particularly for real-world and combined degradations. The contribution connects user control with automatic image assessment inside a single adaptive fusion process.
neurips-2025-controlfusion-a-controllabl.tldr: ControlFusion combines text instructions and visual degradation assessment to adapt image restoration and fusion to compound image damage.

paragraphs: Dense associative memory networks retrieve stored patterns through an energy function whose low points correspond to memories. This paper proposes a different energy function, log-sum-ReLU, inspired by optimal kernel density estimation. It uses the Epanechnikov kernel in place of the log-sum-exponential construction commonly used in these networks.

The proposed energy supports exact retrieval with exponential memory capacity without requiring exponential separation functions. Its distinctive feature is that it also produces many additional local minima while preserving perfect recovery of the stored patterns. Thus, the model can accommodate extra emergent memories alongside accurate access to its original patterns, a combination the authors identify as new in this literature.

Empirically, the new energy yields significantly more local minima with log-likelihood values comparable to those of log-sum-exponential models. Analysis on image datasets finds emergent memories displaying some novelty and creativity. These observations suggest possible generative uses as well as large-scale storage applications; the generative potential is presented as a promising implication of the observed memories.
neurips-2025-dense-associative-memory-wi.tldr: A new associative-memory energy function preserves exact pattern retrieval while producing many additional, potentially useful emergent memories.

paragraphs: Branch-and-Cut solves mixed-integer optimization problems through a sequence of decisions, including which node to explore, which cuts to select, and which variable to branch on. These choices strongly affect efficiency. As researchers replace manually tuned heuristics with learned policies, a central question is how much training data is needed for those policies to generalize.

This paper establishes sample complexity bounds for policies whose decision scores have a specified piecewise polynomial structure. The restriction is useful because it covers more than linear scoring rules: it also includes neural network architectures such as those using ReLU activations. The analysis therefore encompasses models studied in both established theoretical work and contemporary practical research.

The result supplies a common mathematical framework for reasoning about learning these sequential policies from finite datasets. Its guarantees depend on the stated structural class of scoring functions. The authors also extend the scope beyond Branch-and-Cut to fairly general sequential decision problems, making the contribution relevant to learning decision procedures as well as optimization heuristics.
neurips-2025-generalization-guarantees-f.tldr: The paper bounds the training data needed for Branch-and-Cut policies with piecewise polynomial scores, including relevant neural network policies.

paragraphs: HALO targets the difficulty of fine-tuning language models using low-precision arithmetic throughout their large matrix multiplications. Pretrained models can contain unusually large weights, activations, and output gradients. These outliers make quantization difficult because low-precision representations must accommodate them while retaining enough information for accurate learning.

The method places Hadamard rotations strategically in both forward and backward computation to mitigate those outliers. It combines these transformations with optimized computational kernels and fully sharded data parallel integration for low-precision communication. Together, these components enable all large matrix multiplications in both passes to run at reduced precision, addressing the computation and communication sides of training.

On LLaMa fine-tuning tasks, HALO reports results close to full-precision training while supporting INT8 and FP6 arithmetic. Full fine-tuning on RTX 4090 GPUs achieves up to a 1.41-fold end-to-end speedup. The framework also supports parameter-efficient fine-tuning. These findings demonstrate practical accuracy and speed benefits in the evaluated settings, connecting quantization design to measured training performance.
neurips-2025-halo-hadamard-assisted-lowe.tldr: HALO uses Hadamard rotations and optimized execution to enable accurate INT8 and FP6 language-model fine-tuning with measured speed gains.

paragraphs: This paper investigates how a small number of hidden dynamical variables can produce neural recordings that appear high-dimensional. The authors construct an analytically solvable recurrent network whose dynamics reduce exactly to a low-dimensional system, even though its activity requires many linear dimensions to represent. The model shows that these two descriptions can coexist.

The explanation depends on nonlinear processing by individual neurons. The authors use spectral theory to show that the covariance eigenspectrum alone cannot determine latent dimensionality when neuronal responses are nonlinear. They then develop Neural Cross-Encoder, an interpretable nonlinear latent-variable method, to investigate the hidden structure of recorded activity more directly.

In mouse visual cortex, their analysis reduces responses to drifting gratings and spontaneous activity to low-dimensional latents, but does not do so for natural-image responses. The findings therefore depend on the recording condition. They support the view that some high-dimensional activity, including activity without a stimulus, can arise from low-dimensional dynamics transformed nonlinearly by neurons.
neurips-2025-high-dimensional-neuronal-a.tldr: A solvable neural model and recording analysis show how nonlinear neurons can turn low-dimensional latent dynamics into high-dimensional activity.

paragraphs: Inferring interactions between brain areas is difficult when neuronal activity also changes with unobserved behavior or internal states. These background changes vary across trials and can contaminate estimates of functional coupling. GLM-Transformer addresses this problem by modeling individual-neuron dynamics and interactions between populations within a shared framework.

The model combines a point-process generalized linear model for spike trains with a Transformer-based variational autoencoder. The autoencoder captures changing latent influences on individual neurons, while interpretable regression terms estimate directed coupling between populations. A low-rank structure on the coupling effects improves scalability, allowing the interaction component to remain manageable as the population model grows.

On synthetic datasets and mechanistic simulations, the method recovers known coupling and remains robust to shared background fluctuations. Applied to the Allen Institute Visual Coding dataset, it identifies feedforward pathways consistent with established visual hierarchies. These results support using flexible latent models to account for background variation while retaining an interpretable description of functional interactions across brain areas.
neurips-2025-identifying-interactions-ac.tldr: GLM-Transformer separates flexible background neural dynamics from interpretable coupling estimates to better identify interactions across brain areas.

paragraphs: This paper asks why models adopt different in-context learning strategies during training. For models trained on mixtures of tasks, it describes behavior using Bayesian predictors: one emphasizes previously seen tasks, while another represents the underlying task distribution. These correspond to memorizing and generalizing approaches to interpreting examples in context.

The authors place these strategies inside a hierarchical Bayesian framework. Pretraining updates the relative probabilities of the strategies, and inference combines their predictions using those probabilities. Under assumptions about neural learning dynamics, strategy preference reflects both predictive loss and implementation complexity. This makes the explanation sensitive to computational constraints as well as fit to the training data.

The framework almost perfectly predicts Transformer next-token outputs throughout the studied training process without accessing model weights. It also predicts a superlinear increase in the time required to shift from generalization to memorization as task diversity grows. The contribution is an explanatory account in which changing behavior follows from competition among strategies with different losses and complexities.
neurips-2025-in-context-learning-strateg.tldr: A hierarchical Bayesian account explains changing in-context learning strategies through tradeoffs between predictive loss and strategy complexity.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised learning often supplements scarce labeled examples with model-generated labels for unlabeled data. When classes are imbalanced, many methods assume a particular class distribution in the unlabeled pool. Controllable Pseudo-label Generation addresses the more realistic case where that distribution is unknown and may take an arbitrary form.

CPG progressively admits reliable pseudo-labels into the labeled dataset while controlling the resulting class distribution. It then adjusts classifier logits using that known distribution to construct a Bayes-optimal classifier. The improved classifier supplies the next round of pseudo-labels, creating an iterative cycle. Additional components adapt augmentation by class and use an auxiliary branch to draw on all labeled and unlabeled samples.

The authors prove that this cycle can substantially reduce generalization error under certain conditions. Benchmark evaluations show consistent improvements, with reported accuracy gains reaching 15.97% over state-of-the-art methods. The approach matters because it bases classifier adjustment on a distribution it controls, reducing dependence on a predefined description of the unlabeled data.
neurips-2025-keep-it-on-a-leash-controll.tldr: CPG controls which pseudo-labels enter training so imbalanced semi-supervised learning can handle unknown unlabeled class distributions.

paragraphs: Visual counterfactual explanations identify small input changes that would alter a model’s prediction. Their usefulness depends on producing meaningful alternative examples. Existing methods can struggle with vanishing gradients, discontinuous latent representations, and discrepancies between a model’s learned decision boundary and the boundary implied by ground-truth labels.

LeapFactual uses conditional flow matching to generate reliable counterfactuals even when learned and true boundaries differ. The method does not require the explained system to have a differentiable loss. This broadens its reach to human-in-the-loop settings, including tasks where human annotators participate in assigning labels.

Experiments on benchmark and real-world datasets report accurate counterfactuals that remain within the data distribution and provide actionable insights. The authors also observe that counterfactual samples whose labels agree with ground truth can improve a model when reused as training data. The findings connect explanation quality with a possible route to model improvement: generated alternatives can reveal meaningful changes and, in the reported experiments, supply useful additional examples.
neurips-2025-leapfactual-reliable-visual.tldr: LeapFactual uses conditional flow matching to generate meaningful visual counterfactuals, including for nondifferentiable and human-in-the-loop systems.

paragraphs: A junta is a function whose output depends on only a small subset of its input variables. This paper studies learning such functions when the inputs follow a Markov random field, which can represent dependencies among variables. The target functions depend on O(log n) variables, and the proposed algorithm runs in polynomial time.

The guarantee uses smoothed analysis: randomness perturbs only the external field of the Markov random field. This condition is part of the result. It extends earlier work for smoothed product distributions, where variables are independent, to the broader setting in which the graphical model can contain edges representing dependencies.

The algorithm proceeds in two phases. An unsupervised phase learns structure, and a greedy supervised phase then learns the target function. This links knowledge of the input distribution’s dependency structure to the prediction task. The authors identify it as the first downstream supervised-learning application of algorithms for learning undirected graphical-model structure, giving those structural methods a concrete role in efficient function learning.
neurips-2025-learning-juntas-under-marko.tldr: The paper gives a polynomial-time algorithm for logarithmic-size juntas under Markov random fields with randomly perturbed external fields.

paragraphs: Magical addresses the task of rewriting technical medical content for broader audiences while preserving its meaning. Training examples from different sources can demand different accessible writing styles. The authors’ exploratory experiments find that standard low-rank adaptation struggles to meet both semantic fidelity and stylistic diversity requirements in this heterogeneous setting.

The proposed architecture separates shared summarization from style-specific generation within LoRA. A shared matrix A supports abstractive summarization, while multiple isolated B matrices support different lay-language styles. A semantic invariance constraint limits shifts in A’s semantic subspace. A recommendation-guided switching interface selects among the B matrices to adapt the generated style.

Across three real-world datasets, Magical consistently outperforms prompting, standard LoRA, and recent LoRA variants, while reporting a 31.66% reduction in trainable parameters. The design matters because its shared and specialized components directly address the two demands of the task: preserving scientific content and expressing it in varied accessible forms. The experiments support this division of responsibilities for multi-source medical rewriting.
neurips-2025-magical-medical-lay-languag.tldr: Magical separates shared medical summarization from selectable lay-language styles to improve fidelity and accessibility with fewer trainable parameters.

paragraphs: Estimating a changing hidden state becomes difficult when the system is nonlinear and uncertainty is non-Gaussian. The Max Entropy Moment Kalman Filter focuses on polynomial systems and addresses three connected problems: representing complex beliefs, accommodating noise distributions, and removing dependence on past states as new observations arrive.

The method represents beliefs with maximum-entropy distributions constrained by moments. As the number of moment constraints increases, this representation can asymptotically approximate almost any distribution. Process and observation noise use the same representation. To advance a belief through time, the filter propagates moments through the polynomial process model and reconstructs a distribution from them.

This procedure avoids the symbolic integration that would generally make marginalizing past states intractable. Every step, including extracting a point estimate, can be formulated as convex optimization. The authors demonstrate the filter on challenging robotics tasks, including localization with unknown data association. The contribution is a tractable filtering framework that expands the kinds of uncertainty represented while retaining the stated focus on polynomial dynamics.
neurips-2025-max-entropy-moment-kalman-f.tldr: MEM-KF propagates moments and reconstructs maximum-entropy beliefs to filter polynomial systems with complex, non-Gaussian uncertainty.

paragraphs: ParScale explores improving language models by increasing parallel computation during training and inference. It applies P different learnable transformations to an input, runs the model on these versions in parallel, and dynamically combines the outputs. The parallel streams reuse existing model parameters, providing another way to allocate computation for improved performance.

The authors propose a scaling law and validate it through large-scale pretraining. Their results relate P parallel streams to parameter scaling of order log P, with better inference efficiency. For equivalent performance improvements, the reported examples require up to 22 times less additional memory and six times less additional latency than parameter scaling.

The method can also adapt an existing pretrained model through post-training on a small quantity of tokens, reducing the training budget needed to introduce parallel scaling. These findings suggest a potential route to stronger models in resource-constrained deployment settings. The central contribution is the demonstrated relationship between shared-parameter parallel computation, predictive performance, and the incremental costs of memory and latency.
neurips-2025-parallel-scaling-law-for-la.tldr: ParScale improves language models through parallel, shared-parameter streams, with reported memory and latency advantages over parameter scaling.

paragraphs: R&D-Agent(Q) automates quantitative research by coordinating the development of predictive factors and models. The motivation is that financial prediction involves many changing variables, while research pipelines often handle factor discovery and model development separately. The framework treats their joint improvement as an iterative research and implementation process.

During the Research stage, agents set goal-aligned prompts, formulate hypotheses using domain knowledge, and translate them into tasks. During Development, the Co-STEER code-generation agent implements those tasks, which are executed in real-market backtests. Feedback evaluates the outcomes and guides the next iteration, while a multi-armed bandit scheduler adaptively chooses research directions.

The reported experiments achieve up to twice the annualized returns of classical factor libraries while using 70% fewer factors, and outperform state-of-the-art deep time-series models on real markets. These are empirical outcomes of the evaluated strategies and backtests. The results support coordinated factor–model optimization as a way to combine predictive accuracy with strategy robustness while automating more of the research workflow.
neurips-2025-r-d-agent-quant-a-multi-age.tldr: R&D-Agent(Q) coordinates research, code generation, backtesting, and feedback to jointly optimize financial factors and prediction models.

paragraphs: Few-shot segmentation asks a model to outline objects from previously unseen categories using only a few annotated examples. Success requires matching objects by semantic meaning across images and producing accurate masks. SAM2 already offers strong mask generation and feature matching, making it a useful starting point for this task.

The authors find that SAM2’s features contain rich semantic information despite class-agnostic pretraining. However, this information is mixed with cues tailored to object tracking, which hinders tasks requiring higher-level semantic understanding. SANSA makes the existing semantic structure explicit and adapts SAM2 for few-shot segmentation with minimal task-specific changes.

SANSA reports state-of-the-art results on few-shot benchmarks designed to test generalization and outperforms generalist methods in the in-context setting. It also supports interaction through points, boxes, and scribbles, while being substantially faster and more compact than prior approaches. The findings show that making existing semantics accessible can extend a segmentation model’s capabilities without requiring a large task-specific redesign.
neurips-2025-sansa-unleashing-the-hidden.tldr: SANSA exposes semantic structure already present in SAM2 to enable efficient segmentation of unseen categories from a few examples.

paragraphs: This paper argues that convincing behavior alone is insufficient for useful language-model simulations of society. Agents may produce plausible responses from demographic prompts while lacking coherent beliefs, causal reasoning, or a traceable account of why their responses change. Those shortcomings matter when a simulation is intended to represent deliberation or responses to interventions.

The authors propose Generative Minds, a conceptual modeling paradigm informed by cognitive science. It emphasizes structured representations of beliefs and reasoning that can be revised and traced. The intended shift is toward agents whose behavior can be understood through an internal account of thought, supporting analysis of how beliefs and decisions relate.

They also introduce RECAP, an evaluation framework for reasoning fidelity. It assesses causal traceability, grounding in demographic information, and consistency under interventions. Together, the modeling proposal and benchmark define what cognitively grounded social agents should represent and how to assess them. The contribution is a conceptual and evaluative foundation for social simulation, with the argument centered on reasoning quality beyond surface plausibility.
neurips-2025-simulating-society-requires.tldr: GenMinds and RECAP propose structured beliefs and traceable reasoning as foundations for evaluating language-model social simulations.

paragraphs: ThinkLite-VL investigates how selecting training examples can make visual reasoning improvement more data-efficient. The central idea is that reinforcement fine-tuning benefits from examples that require substantial reasoning but remain solvable. The models improve through reinforcement fine-tuning alone, without knowledge distillation from another model.

The authors repurpose Monte Carlo Tree Search to estimate difficulty from the number of reasoning iterations needed to solve an example. From 70,000 open-source examples covering mathematics, natural images, and charts, they select 11,000 for a 7B model and 7,500 for a 72B model. These subsets supply focused training challenges for the corresponding Qwen2.5-VL base models.

Both resulting models significantly outperform their bases across eight visual reasoning benchmarks. ThinkLite-VL-7B reports a 7% average improvement and a MathVista score of 75.1; the 72B version reaches 79.7 on MathVista. The findings support difficulty-based selection as an effective route to self-improvement with relatively little training data, with the reported gains tied to examples that encourage deeper, successful reasoning.
neurips-2025-sota-with-less-mcts-guided-.tldr: ThinkLite-VL uses tree search to select challenging but solvable examples, achieving strong visual reasoning gains with small training subsets.

paragraphs: Sparc3D addresses detail loss and computational cost in high-resolution 3D generation. Meshes are unstructured, while dense volumetric grids become expensive as resolution grows. Existing pipelines can also lose information when their variational autoencoders move between mismatched representations before a latent diffusion model generates new shapes.

The framework combines Sparcubes, a sparse deformable marching-cubes representation, with Sparconv-VAE. Sparcubes places signed-distance and deformation fields on a sparse cube structure to construct surfaces at 1024³ resolution, supporting arbitrary topology and differentiable optimization. Sparconv-VAE uses sparse convolution throughout, keeping its representation modality consistent during compression and reconstruction.

The authors report near-lossless reconstruction and state-of-the-art fidelity on difficult shapes, including open surfaces, disconnected pieces, and intricate geometry. They also report lower training and inference costs and compatibility with latent diffusion generation. The approach matters because it addresses the representation and compression stages together: preserving detailed geometry at those stages supplies a stronger foundation for scalable, high-resolution synthesis.
neurips-2025-sparc3d-sparse-representati.tldr: Sparc3D combines sparse surface construction and a modality-consistent autoencoder to preserve fine 3D detail efficiently.

paragraphs: A Schrödinger bridge connects two probability distributions through a stochastic process with minimal energy modification. The Sinkhorn bridge estimates such a process using optimal transport inside time-dependent stochastic dynamics. This paper studies the practical setting where neither endpoint distribution is fully known and only finite samples from each are available.

The main result bounds squared total variation error at intermediate Sinkhorn iterations by O(1/m + 1/n + r^(2k)), where m and n are endpoint sample sizes, k is the iteration count, and r lies between zero and one. The expression separates finite-sample contributions from a term that decreases geometrically as the algorithm runs.

This separation gives guidance on allocating effort: more iterations reduce the iteration term, while larger datasets reduce the sampling terms. The authors also identify connections that extend their results to several representative bridge estimators under specific settings. The contribution supplies finite-sample justification for partially completed Sinkhorn computations and clarifies how data quantity and iteration count jointly affect the statistical guarantee.
neurips-2025-statistical-analysis-of-the.tldr: The paper bounds Sinkhorn bridge estimation error using both endpoint sample sizes and the number of algorithm iterations.

paragraphs: Noise-as-Watermark methods embed identifying information in the initial Gaussian noise used to generate a diffusion image. Detection reverses generation to estimate that noise and recover the watermark. The challenge is that constraining noise strongly can improve watermark recovery while reducing the diversity of generated images.

T2SMark introduces Tail-Truncated Sampling to manage this tradeoff. It embeds bits in reliable tail regions of the noise distribution and samples the central region randomly to preserve the latent distribution. Its two-stage design also incorporates a randomly generated session key into both encryption pipelines, supporting diversity in the sampled noise.

The authors evaluate the method on diffusion models with U-Net and DiT backbones and report an optimal balance between watermark robustness and generation diversity in their experiments. The mechanism matters because it assigns information-bearing and freely sampled portions of the noise different roles. This provides a concrete way to strengthen watermark extraction while retaining variability in the generation process.
neurips-2025-t2smark-balancing-robustnes.tldr: T2SMark embeds watermark bits in reliable noise tails and randomizes other components to balance recovery robustness with image diversity.

paragraphs: Persistent homology summarizes how topological features appear and disappear as a geometric scale changes. For large point clouds, constructing the underlying collection of vertices, edges, and higher-dimensional simplices can become prohibitively expensive. Even more scalable alternatives to the widely used Vietoris-Rips construction can leave too many simplices to process.

The Flood complex builds a Delaunay triangulation on a small subset of the points. At a given radius, it includes simplices fully covered by the union of balls centered on the complete point cloud. This flooding process combines ideas from Alpha and Witness complexes, with theoretical properties and a construction suited to GPU parallelization.

Experiments compute persistent homology through dimension two on 3D clouds containing several million points. Object classification evaluations on real and synthetic data provide evidence that this scale matters especially for geometrically or topologically complex objects. Reported performance exceeds other persistent-homology methods and point-cloud neural networks in those evaluations, connecting computational scalability to useful shape information.
neurips-2025-the-flood-complex-large-sca.tldr: The Flood complex enables persistent homology on millions of 3D points, with reported benefits for classifying complex shapes.

paragraphs: Evidential deep learning estimates uncertainty by predicting a distribution over class probabilities. Standard versions use a Dirichlet distribution, providing an efficient representation of uncertainty. This paper argues that the restriction to this distribution family can weaken robustness when the prediction setting becomes complex or unexpected.

Flexible evidential deep learning replaces that family with a flexible Dirichlet distribution, a generalization designed to express a broader range of uncertainty. The model still predicts uncertainty over class probabilities, but has a more adaptable representation. The change directly targets the distributional assumption at the center of the original approach.

The authors establish several theoretical advantages and report state-of-the-art uncertainty quantification across classical, long-tailed, and noisy in-distribution evaluations. These settings examine uncertainty under ordinary conditions, class imbalance, and noise. The results support the claim that a more expressive distribution can improve uncertainty reliability and generalization across challenging evaluated scenarios, addressing a limitation of the original evidential formulation.
neurips-2025-uncertainty-estimation-by-f.tldr: Flexible evidential deep learning broadens the distribution used to model class-probability uncertainty and improves reported uncertainty estimates.

paragraphs: Vad-R1 extends video anomaly detection toward explaining and analyzing unusual events. The authors introduce Video Anomaly Reasoning as a task that requires explicit reasoning before an answer. Their motivation is that existing multimodal approaches often provide shallow descriptions, leaving the interpretation of an anomaly insufficiently developed.

The framework uses a structured Perception-to-Cognition Chain-of-Thought to guide stepwise anomaly analysis. The authors use this structure to build Vad-Reasoning, a dedicated dataset. They also introduce AVA-GRPO, a reinforcement learning algorithm with a self-verification mechanism that explicitly rewards anomaly reasoning while using limited annotations.

Experiments report that Vad-R1 outperforms evaluated open-source and proprietary models on both anomaly detection and anomaly reasoning tasks. The contribution combines a task definition, a reasoning structure, a dataset, and a training method around the same objective. The reported gains suggest that directly training structured analysis and self-verification can strengthen anomaly interpretation while also improving performance on the associated detection task.
neurips-2025-vad-r1-towards-video-anomal.tldr: Vad-R1 combines structured anomaly reasoning, a dedicated dataset, and self-verifying reinforcement learning to improve video anomaly analysis.
